title: Record date pay scales and the Petrillo trust fund case
summary: He recalls dates paying $33.33 and rising to $48, $55 and $75, and a union case over the trust fund that paid him about $7,000.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Maybe some of them were. A guy like Erroll, he wouldn't have paid that much attention to it. But some of us were aware that something might have been happening. But during those times record dates paid so little, even for the times... I think a record date was thirty three dollars and thirty three cents or some ridiculous amount like that.
Of course, there was more money then than now.
It meant more then than it does now. Then finally, they got it up to $48, and then $55, and $75. I think it's probably $150 by now, twenty years later.

But a lot of this had to do with Petrillo. Norman Granz mentioned this at one time, way back, that the record companies were prepared to pay $100 for dates way back, and Petrillo accepted a lesser amount and put it in a trust fund. That's when we had a case against the union, which we won. I remember getting about $7,000 out of that.
Oh, that was over twenty years ago. That's when Petrillo resigned and someone else took his place. Those are the facts.
